Rezankand (H67)

Region (English scoring-table region): South Aelantir.

In a sentence: A Sun Elf holy-knight expedition crosses the sea to return to its ancestral homeland, free slaves, and build a new home—while confronting the question of whether “redeemers” might become conquerors.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100 | Autocracy 77/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 51/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 91/100) | Pluralism 75/100. The v2.1 values assessment is Good (72/100), with a mixed trajectory. Freeing slaves, protecting Taychendi Ruinborn communities, and building a multi-ethnic Dry Coast have clear positive evidence. However, replacing local judgment with a mission of holy light, religious-military expansion, and burning the jungle reduce restraint and recognition of others' agency. War and theocracy are not penalized in themselves.

Narrative: Extremely high | Mission-tree length: Long (44 missions available to H67, of which 15 are also available to H66) | Verified version: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Extremely high | Degree of confinement: High (overseas expedition, religious events, and continental wars) | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: Extremely high

The Campaign Does Not Begin as Rezankand in 1444

H67 is not a country on the 1444 map. The usual route begins with political upheaval in Bulwar and the expedition phase of the Jaherian Exemplars (H66): an organization of Sun-worshipping elven warriors, mages, and followers that sails to South Aelantir in search of its ancestral homeland, believing it has a duty to oppose “darkness.” The offline English Wiki's setting history says they left Eltílnór, reached Taychend in 1516, and established Rezankand on the Dry Coast in 1562. These dates explain the characters and migration; a player's formation date depends on the campaign and is not a hard requirement. In the current scripts, H66 and H67 share several prologue missions. Completing the chain to establish a country on the Dry Coast invokes the formation effect that switches to H67, after which the new Tag continues with its dedicated missions. The figure of 44 is the number available to H67; do not add the 15 shared missions again to claim 59.

Who Decides Where the Light Falls?

The most distinctive early phase is the expedition into Taychend and the withdrawal to the Dry Coast: make contact with local powers, expose slavery, bring along people who wish to migrate, and build new coastal settlements. Later missions expand the knightly orders and the Order of Exemplars, incorporate Taychendi Ruinborn Elves who remained in their ancestral homeland, local humans, and other peoples, then return to Taychend to challenge slavers and warlords. The development diary explicitly says the old tree was reworked and the current route focuses on freeing slaves rather than simply seizing wealth. That matches the local mission text about “long-lost brothers” and the Exemplars' return.

The offline Wiki's setting history does not portray the Exemplars as flawless heroes who never made mistakes. The expedition and local anti-slavery groups opposed the same institution, yet clashed over timing, mutual suspicion, and control of cities. The Exemplars also established footholds with the authorization of local rulers before falling out with former allies. The reworked “liberation” theme therefore does not mean that local people always welcome them. The political conflict asks two questions at once: when should enslaved people be free, and who has the right to decide what that freedom looks like on their behalf?

Rezankand wields more than swords: it studies Precursor relics, magical inscriptions, and flying devices, joining a sacred mission to artifice. Another main thread enters the Effelai Jungle and uses fire against plant consciousness regarded as “evil darkness.” There is epic grandeur here, but also an ethical edge. Opposition to slavery, sheltering refugees, and recognizing Taychendi Ruinborn Elves as kin are clearly positive actions. Yet the claim “we will decide what liberation means for you,” religious conversion, and ecological burning can conflict with local agency. The values profile therefore describes the country as good but contested, rather than treating every war as virtuous. The development diary similarly uses indigenous objections to the “foreign savior” to highlight this tension.

In gameplay, Dry Coast settlement and raids into Taychend are objectives with different rhythms. The early expedition cannot remain inland indefinitely: bring people, knowledge, and resources back to the coast, then use the new country as a base for the next campaign. Mid- and late-game technological and magical research is more than a handful of bonuses; Precursor relics and flying platforms connect the old-world Sun Cult with the New World legacy, and the country grows from a band of holy knights into a transcontinental power with a complex technological system.

This country suits players who enjoy holy knights, overseas state-building, liberation narratives, Order of Exemplars missions, ruin research, and long campaigns of conquest. It is a poor fit if you want to remain small and focused, reject religious-military expansion, or want to control H67 directly from the start. Player posts range from high praise for the overseas expedition to complaints that later missions were repetitive in the old version. The latter predate the rework and do not assess the writing of the current 44 available missions.

The results card places it between magic and artifice because the mission tree uses both, not because neither matters. Its high intensity score signals that late-game aircraft, inscriptions, and order magic are central to the country's identity.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Rezankand (H67) — Rezankandi Ideas

Set ID: H67_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = H67
    }

Rezankandi Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Heretic tolerance: +2 (tolerance_heathen; raw value 2).

1. Orders with a State

Founded by members of the Order of Exemplars, Rezankand is a country dominated by its various Holy Orders, who work together in the fight against Darkness. Rezankand’s Ruler is the Herald of Light, elected by the Conclave of Dawn, an assembly composed of the most senior members from each order, regardless of race.

Rezankand has many civilian and military Holy Orders, some inherited from Bulwar, but the vast majority were established to fulfill the needs of the new country, filling the same role that secular institutions have in other countries.

The main civilian orders are the Order of Judges in charge of the judicial system, and the Servants of Surael which represent the interests of the many artisan guilds. The most influential military orders are the Order of Avengers, tasked with bringing war to the Effelai, and the Order of Sundancers, composed of engineers, artificiers, mages and soldiers who are in charge of the Migrant Ship Diranhriá.

  • All estates' loyalty equilibrium: +5% (all_estate_loyalty_equilibrium; raw value 0.05).

  • Establish order cost: -15% (establish_order_cost; raw value -0.15).

2. Dawn Elves

Believing that purifying the Darkness of South Aelantir can protect the Garden of Surael, the Rezankandi are determined to triumph in Aelantir, and they are not alone in this endeavor. Contrary to other countries who make distinctions between Migrant Elves and Ruinborn Elves, in Rezankand they are all considered a member of the same race, and those who follow the Sun Cult are known as Dawn Elf.

Most Elves make an effort to join one of the Holy Orders during the course of their long lives, of which the Exemplars is most prominent. They then go on to train and perfect their martial skills, even if they do not intend to take any of the vows. This also serves to fulfill the duty that all Elves feel, that one should always be prepared to fight back against the coming Darkness.

  • Possible advisors: +1 (advisor_pool; raw value 1).

  • Number of accepted cultures: +2 (num_accepted_cultures; raw value 2).

3. Cult of Exemplary

While Bulwari temples converted to the Jadd and proclaimed the Divine-herald as head of the faith, Rezankand maintained the traditional autocephaly of the temples. In the mid-1500s, the Council of Jaherdin enacted multiple reforms within the Cult, the most important being that Jaher’s mission, and thus divinity, had been passed down to the Exemplars and the other Holy Orders of Rezankand. While understanding the logic of the founders of the New Sun Cult, the council decided that tasking the entire Sun Elven race with the duties of being a Chosen was unwise, and that from this moment, only those who want to protect and guide the Faithful by being paragons through example should bear the burden of Chosenhood.

  • Yearly Army Professionalism: +0.3% (yearly_army_professionalism; raw value 0.003).

4. Darkness in the West

The Rezankandi never forgave the Kalavendhi for the Betrayal of Urvand. Both groups had been allied against the Larankara, with the promise that the Kalavendhi would abandon slavery and give up lands in the south for the Exemplars to settle. This however was a vile deception, and after the alliance stormed the Larankara capital and installed Tasheladar as a puppet ruler, the Kalavendhi and the Larankara turned against the Exemplars, forcing them to retreat back to Katelperai.

Since then, animosity has run rampant between Rezankand and the Taychendi, with Rezankand invading the region several times from their base in Katelperai. The Rezankandi believe that the rulers of Taychend are corrupted by the Darkness, and thus need to be eradicated in order to liberate their people from oppression.

  • Unjustified demands: -20% (unjustified_demands; raw value -0.2).

5. Karodir's Legacy

Karodir of Varamhar was the only Sun Elf king that survived the Jaddari conquest of the Suran Plain, fleeing with the Exemplars to Aelantir after being freed from Akalšes. He accompanied the Exemplar expedition to Katelperai and Nanru Nakar, where he learned from the Taychendi and from the Precursor ruins.

In the following decades, he focused on the study of magic and precursor knowledge, trying to decipher the relics and artifacts found in Taychend and the Diranhriá. To gain help in this endeavor, he established the House of Knowledge of Jaherdin, also known as the White Phoenix Academy, a center of learning and development, from where Karodir and his students managed to pioneer artificery in Rezankand and South Aelantir, using their knowledge to repair the systems of the Diranhriá, and even to recreate some of the Precursor Artifacts found in Taychend.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Sundancer

The Diranhriá was Jaher’s precursor ship, a mighty dreadnought of the Precursor Empire, that, according to the few surviving records, fought in the war against the Dwarves, destroying half of old Ovdal Tûngr’s fleet with a single barrage. When the Sun Elves fled from South Aelantir during the Day of Ashen Skies, they took the Sundancer with them, turning the dreadnought into a Migrant Ship.

After the founding of the Phoenix Empire, the Diranhriá was retrofitted again into a battleship and became the flagship of the Sunset fleet, until the ship was damaged when Vulzin the Red charged with the ship against the sea monster Wanamur. The ship was never fully repaired, and once it was moved to Elizna, remained dry-docked there until the Exemplars made use of the vessel for their voyage to South Aelantir.

Karodir managed to repair some of the ship’s intricate magic systems, restoring the Sundancer’s armament to half power, and that power was more than enough for the Dirhariá to decimate the Anbennarian fleet during the invasion of Malatel.

  • Naval combat bonus off owned coasts: +1 (own_coast_naval_combat_bonus; raw value 1).

7. The Western Garden

When the Exemplars and the Bulwari settled the Dry Coast, they quickly started to transform the land. By constructing agricultural canals, roads, and securing their border with the Effelai, as the untamed jungle is considered tainted by Darkness, this was seen as restoring civilization and order by the Sun Cult. These new cities were decorated with magnificent gardens, and the Conclave of Dawn terraces filled with flora from Aelantir and Bulwar.

They built an unwalled garden of a country, as no one expected the Effelai to expand its influence, however during the Blooming, the jungle’s wrath was unleashed. It started with whispers and rumors about how the Darkness deep within the dense vines and foliage was against our presence in Aelantir, and when the Jungle took control of the wonderful Rezankandi gardens, the people suffered as they had to burn them in order to stop further spreading of the infestation. A tragedy that convinced the Rezankandi that if they wanted to stay in Aelantir, the Effelai had to be burned to the ground, and its Darkness purified from Aelantir.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.10).

Jaherian Exemplars (H66) — Sun Elf Ideas

Set ID: sun_elf_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        primary_culture = sun_elf
    }

Sun Elf Traditions

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -20% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.2).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

1. Purity of Blood

Unlike our Moon Elf cousins to the west we are proud and protective of our elvish blood and don't weaken it with miscegenation, and such remain pure and true heirs of elvenkind.

  • Prestige: +0.5 (prestige; raw value 0.5).

2. Flying Chariots

Bulwar has always been famous for its sky platforms, flying chariots, piloted by a mage with two others flinging death from above. They are not only very handy in bombarding compact formations before they reach our troops but also in scouting.

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Land fire damage: +10% (fire_damage; raw value 0.10).

3. Discriminatory Magical Schooling

We need to prevent any possible rebels to master the arts of magic. We must kick any potentially 'unreliable' elements out of magical schools.

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

4. Centuries of Experience

Due to our long lives our administrators have lots of time to learn the ins and outs of running a country.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

5. Lavish Courts

Our luxurious palaces have such good reputations that we tend to drown in potential advisors wishing to work in them. It appears decadence has its advantages.

  • Possible advisors: +1 (advisor_pool; raw value 1).

6. Long Educations

The education of our people is the backbone of our state. As we can accumulate a lot of it in our long lives, we can produce the most influential poets, statesmen, natural philosophers and scholars.

  • Technology cost: -10% (technology_cost; raw value -0.10).

7. Experienced Plotters

Our kingdoms are known its vying dynastic families and intrigue. If we manage to turn the experience in plotting we gained from this outwards we have a great tool in our hands.

  • Spy network construction: +20% (spy_offence; raw value 0.2).

Sun Elf Ambition

  • Leaders without upkeep: +1 (free_leader_pool; raw value 1).
